title: Geometric fibre density of strict-henselian sections
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], equipped with a section $e:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume that every residue-field fibre of $f$ is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-residue-field]. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$, every algebraically closed extension field $\Omega$ of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and every nonempty open subset $W\subset X_\Omega=X\times_R\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product], there is an $R$-section $a:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ whose induced $\Omega$-point lies in $W$. Equivalently, the values in $X_\Omega(\Omega)$ of all $R$-sections are Zariski dense in every geometric fibre. No group structure on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated section-density input, motivated by Slicing smooth morphisms (Tag 055U, lemma-etale-nbhd-dominates-smooth) and henselian lifting. That Stacks lemma is not itself the density assertion; the present unsplit node includes the additional density assertion.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, let $s$ be its closed point and $k=R/\mathfrak m$. By the smooth normal-form node choose an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $e(s)$ and an etale $S$-map $\pi:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$. The base neighbourhood in that node is all of $S$: an open containing the closed point of a local spectrum contains every prime. The same observation applied to $e^{-1}(U)$ gives $e:S\to U$. Write $\alpha=\pi e\in R^d$. For the given $\mathfrak q,\Omega$, the open $U_\Omega\subseteq X_\Omega$ contains $e_\Omega$ and is nonempty. Geometric irreducibility makes $X_\Omega$ irreducible, so $V=U_\Omega\cap W$ is a nonempty open of the irreducible affine scheme $U_\Omega$.

source.place: Agent-written section-density argument using Tag 054L (lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space), Tag 03J2 (lemma-image-nowhere-dense-quasi-finite), and strict-henselian etale lifting as in etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian).

proof.text: The affine base-change lemma makes $\pi_\Omega:U_\Omega\to\mathbf A^d_\Omega$ etale. Its affine ring map is finite type and quasi-finite at every prime by the etale ring-map lemma; the ring-map definition says that every point of every fibre is isolated, and the scheme definition therefore makes $\pi_\Omega$ quasi-finite as a scheme morphism. The closed set $Z=U_\Omega\setminus V$ is nowhere dense: in an irreducible space every nonempty open meets $V$. Apply the quasi-finite nowhere-dense-image node to $Z$. Thus $O=\mathbf A^d_\Omega\setminus\overline{\pi_\Omega(Z)}$ is nonempty open. Choose a nonempty principal open $D(P)\subseteq O$, with $0\ne P\in\Omega[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$. Principal opens form the defining basis of the affine spectrum. Consequently every point of $U_\Omega$ whose coordinate vector evaluates $P$ nontrivially lies in $V$.

proof.text: We will use the elementary polynomial test: if $D_1,\ldots,D_d$ are infinite subsets of a field $L$, no nonzero polynomial in $L[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ vanishes on their product. Induct on $d$: choose the first $d-1$ coordinates where a nonzero coefficient in the last variable does not vanish, then avoid the finitely many roots of that nonzero one-variable polynomial in $D_d$. For $d=0$ a nonzero constant already has nonzero value. The field $k$ is infinite. Indeed it is separably closed by strict henselianity; if it had cardinality $N$, the polynomial $T^N-T-1$ would have derivative $-1$ and no root in $k$, contrary to separable closedness.

proof.text: First suppose $\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak m$. Choose $t\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak q$. The domain $R/\mathfrak q$ is infinite, since it surjects onto the infinite field $k$. Multiplication by the nonzero image of $t$ is injective, so the image of $\mathfrak m$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\subseteq\Omega$ is infinite. For each coordinate, the image $D_i$ of $\alpha_i+\mathfrak m$ in $\Omega$ is therefore infinite. The polynomial test supplies $r_i\in\alpha_i+\mathfrak m$ such that $P(r_1,\ldots,r_d)\ne0$ after mapping to $\Omega$. Form $E=U\times_{\mathbf A^d_S,r}S$. The affine base-change lemma makes $E\to S$ etale. Its closed fibre is nonempty, because $r\bmod\mathfrak m=\alpha\bmod\mathfrak m$ and $e(s)$ lies above that vector. The strict-henselian etale-neighbourhood section node gives a section $S\to E$. Its composite $a:S\to U\to X$ is an $R$-section with $\pi a=r$. Its $\Omega$-value evaluates $P$ nontrivially, so Step 2 places it in $V\subseteq W$.

proof.text: Every prime of the local ring is contained in $\mathfrak m$, so Steps 4 and 5 cover all primes. They show that the values of $R$-sections meet every nonempty open of each $X_\Omega$, which is exactly Zariski density. The argument uses only the given section and smooth charts, and imposes no group structure.
